   in fusion ([S0196](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3561920),
   [S0203](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/add16e),
   [S0207](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2026.115267)).

*Inference.* Paths 1, 2, and 6 need no new fabrication and no new HSX
campaign beyond data already in hand or bench work on existing dies; they
directly answer the decline letter's specific requests (calibration,
repeatability, comparison table). Paths 3ΓÇô5 are campaign- or
hardware-coupled. Path 7 establishes that the deployment-novelty framing
itself is publishable **if** rigorously documented ΓÇö which is the standard
the manuscript was judged against and missed (┬º6).

---

## 6. The field's validation norms versus the manuscript's current state (mission Q4, Q6)

*External evidence ΓÇö what published fusion-instrumentation work reports:*
itemized uncertainty budgets ([S0152], [S0094](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/aa86fd));
calibration against an independent standard or model ([S0143], [S0137],
[S0148], [S0115]); accuracy versus a stated requirement ([S0148]: 4 mT 2╧â;
[S0144](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/53/4/043009): ~1 mm position
control); environmental qualification as a program ([S0112], [S0114],
[S0153]); and multi-year/multi-pulse stability ([S0068]: ┬▒0.07% over
19,000 pulses). Bandwidth claims are derived and characterized, not
asserted ([S0076](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3246785): 10 kHzΓÇô50 MHz B-dot
characterization; [S0178](https://doi.org/10.3390/s20102929): 200 kHz
in-vessel digital-integration chain).

*Supplied fact.* The manuscript reports one uncalibrated module, V_off
unknown, a 200 V/V gain chain, an asserted (reviewer-questioned) 1 MHz
bandwidth, and temporal correlation with the diamagnetic loop as its
validation (claim baseline C001ΓÇôC005; conflict ledger C6 records that
project 02's "calibrated" language is aspirational ΓÇö bench emulator only,
with an unresolved ~109├ù magnitude anomaly).

*Inference.* Every element of the decline letter maps onto a published,
citable norm; nothing the reviewers asked for is exotic or
disproportionate. Conversely, the manuscript's demonstrated content
(in-vessel survival, real-time shot-resolved response, correlation with an
independent diagnostic) matches what first-deployment papers in other
fields successfully publish ([S0227], [S0230]) ΓÇö *when* accompanied by
calibration/uncertainty documentation. The gap is rigor-of-reporting plus
absolute calibration, not concept validity. **Gap register for stage
`40_experiment`:** absolute calibration + V_off (norm: [S0148], [S0051]);
repeatability across dies (norm: [S0218], [S0068]); uncertainty budget
(norm: [S0152], [S0220]); bandwidth derivation (norm: [S0076]);
conventional-probe comparison (norm: [S0143]; AEIC request); field-unit
presentation (trivial once calibration exists); vector-probe placement
justification for project 03 (norm: [S0210], [S0132]).

---

## 7. Venue-route evidence (mission Q5 ΓÇö evidence only, decision deferred)

*External evidence.* Review of Scientific Instruments is the single most
frequent venue in this ledger (29/231 rows) and routinely publishes exactly
this genre: stellarator in-vessel probe design/characterization
([S0154](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0002193)), Hall-probe deployments in
confinement devices ([S0143], [S0173]), magnetic-diagnostic systems and
integrators ([S0093], [S0106]), and system-integration-as-contribution
([S0226]). The advisor group has a prior RSI sensor paper
([S0006]). Fusion Engineering and Design and Nuclear Fusion carry the
Hall-sensor qualification lineage ([S0148], [S0068], [S0112]); IEEE
Sensors Letters carries the group's own short-format GaN device letters
([S0005]).

*Inference (not a decision).* The literature shows the project's natural
center of gravity ΓÇö in-vessel deployment + calibration + validation against
a computed field ΓÇö is the RSI/FED/NF genre, while the *device-letter* genre
(Sensors Letters) rewards device novelty, which is the axis Reviewer 2
attacked. This is evidence about venue fit, not a recommendation on the
revise-vs-arXiv+RSI route; that comparison, including timing and the
decline letter's resubmission invitation, belongs to stages `20_direction`
and `30_manuscript`. Note on arXiv: preprints are excluded from this
ledger by policy and nothing here evaluates preprint strategy.

---

## 8. Conflicts, disagreements, and unresolved gaps

1. **Reviewer disagreement is real and literature-grounded** (┬º3.2):
   Reviewer 1's novelty judgment holds at the
   application/material-in-context granularity; Reviewer 2's holds at the
   device-technique granularity. Not a contradiction in the evidence ΓÇö a
   fork in claim framing.
2. **Publication-status conflict (Stage 00 C1/C2)** stands: the
   parent-project "2023, published" framing is contradicted by the supplied
   2026 submission/decline records. Nothing found in this stage's
   literature search (no DOI, no published record of the manuscript)
   changes that; the manuscript is treated throughout as unpublished.
3. **Metadata disagreements resolved at merge:** Czech-diacritic author
   renderings (─Äuran ΓåÆ "Duran"; Crossref's own "Boshakova"/"Curan"/"Ceran"
   variants) were resolved against Crossref records for S0070, S0120,
   S0121, S0122; volume/issue enrichments applied to S0095, S0112, S0122,
   S0205; the same-DOI duplicate pairs A0068/B0041 and A0070/B0054 were
   merged into S0068 and S0070. Full audit trail in
   [`01_SOURCE_COVERAGE.md`](01_SOURCE_COVERAGE.md) ┬º3.
4. **Open evidence gaps carried forward** (none closable by more
   searching): no GaN Hall sensor in any confinement device (novelty
   anchor; absence finding); no GaN-specific fusion
   radiation/vacuum/thermal qualification; no HSX Hall-sensor/calibration/
   probe-comparison literature; no quantified spatial-coverage benefit for
   a 2ΓÇô3 axis HSX probe versus existing pickup belts (nearest precedent:
   [S0132]'s 7├ù ambiguity reduction from 80 added coils); no HSX
   discharge-magnetics database at ML-training scale; no published
   quantitative "success bar" for a first-generation academic Hall sensor
   in a stellarator (nearest bars are ITER/JET-grade: [S0148], [S0068]).
5. **What is NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SUPPLIED FILES:** any calibration
   coefficient, V_off value, or absolute-field result for Tim's sensor
   (project 02's bench anomaly is unresolved); the exact-figure
   reproduction of the manuscript's shots (Stage 00 checked file presence
   only); any HSX August-2026 campaign schedule commitment.

---

## 9. Summary against the mission questions

| Mission question | What this review establishes | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 (150+ paper review) | 231 verified peer-reviewed sources across all seven required categories | Done at this stage |
| Q2 (direction publishable/strong?) | Novelty is real but only at a specific claim granularity (first GaN/WBG Hall in-vessel in a confinement device; first Hall sensor in a QHS stellarator); the enabling-rigor gaps are exactly the field's published norms | Evidence assembled; **decision deferred to `20_direction`** |
| Q3 (low-cleanroom novelty) | Seven method classes with mature precedent; calibration/uncertainty, sensor fusion, and reproducibility paths need no new fabrication | Evidence assembled |
| Q4 (manuscript/reviews) | Every reviewer request maps to a citable published norm; both reviewers' novelty positions are literature-consistent at different granularities; "first QHS stellarator" wording needs correction to match [S0128] | Evidence assembled for `30_manuscript` |
| Q5 (venue route) | Genre analysis: deployment+calibration+validation work lives in RSI/FED/NF; device letters reward the axis that was attacked | Evidence only; decision deferred |
| Q6 (next experiment) | Gap register with per-gap published norms (┬º6) | Feeds `40_experiment` |
| Q7 (IP screen) | Dense non-GaN fusion Hall prior art ([S0066]ΓÇô[S0070], [S0112]ΓÇô[S0122]) and decades-old spinning-current art ([S0033]ΓÇô[S0043](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICASIC.2007.4415661)) bound any claim scope | Feeds `50_patent`; no legal conclusion here |
| Q8 (24-month plan) | Data prerequisites and campaign-coupled vs. uncoupled paths (┬º5) | Feeds `60_timeline` |

3	Q2,Is the original direction (GaN Hall-effect magnetic diagnostics for in-situ MCF measurement) publishable and strategically strong?,"Evidence assembled, decision deferred to stage 20_direction. Supporting: no GaN/AlGaN Hall sensor found deployed in any tokamak/stellarator across three independent lanes (novelty anchor); fusion Hall sensing is the field's own chosen steady-state answer (ITER bismuth array, JET InSb 11-yr record), so the sensing concept is validated; GaN offers temperature-stable sensitivity beyond InSb's ~150 C class limit. Opposing: device-level GaN Hall characterization is published prior art (largely from the advisor's own group), so novelty survives only at the application/deployment granularity; a GaN entrant lacks any fusion qualification data comparable to bismuth/antimony/InSb campaigns.",S0004;S0005;S0006;S0012;S0016;S0066;S0067;S0068;S0069;S0070;S0112;S0113;S0114;S0117;S0118;S0120;S0121;S0122;S0143;S0153,strong,"Reviewer 1 ('novel and unique') and Reviewer 2 ('not novel') are both literature-consistent at different claim granularities - application-context vs device-technique; the fork is framing, not evidence.","Absence-of-evidence basis for the first-GaN-in-fusion claim (bounded search, found three times independently); no published success bar for a first-generation academic in-stellarator Hall sensor."
4	Q3,"Prefer paths minimizing new cleanroom work with defensible novelty in application, calibration, measurement architecture, simulation, analysis, inverse methods, or software","Seven method classes have mature, citable precedent and are unapplied on HSX: (1) formal calibration/uncertainty (Bayesian, Allan variance, GUM/MC, traceability); (2) Kalman/Bayesian sensor fusion with HSX's existing diagnostics incl. a W7-AS stellarator precedent; (3) regularized inverse reconstruction; (4) ML/PINN equilibrium reconstruction (stellarator-class precedents exist; HSX-scale training data does not); (5) vector/array design + D-optimality placement for project 03; (6) reproducibility/device-to-device statistics; (7) first-deployment/qualification-as-contribution framing. Classes 1, 2, 6 need no new fabrication and no new campaign.",S0051;S0158;S0159;S0160;S0161;S0164;S0165;S0167;S0168;S0171;S0179;S0180;S0181;S0187;S0188;S0189;S0192;S0193;S0194;S0197;S0199;S0208;S0210;S0214;S0216;S0217;S0218;S0219;S0220;S0221;S0222;S0223;S0225;S0226;S0227;S0229;S0230;S0231,strong,none,No existing HSX discharge-magnetics database at the scale ML precedents trained on (KSTAR: 1118 discharges); no source quantifies the spatial/vector-coverage advantage of a 2-3 axis HSX probe over existing pickup belts.
5	Q4,"Review the submitted IEEE Sensors Letters manuscript, its source files, HSX data, and the 23-Jul-2026 decision/reviewer comments (literature dimension)","Every decline-letter request maps to a published, citable norm: comparison table (assemblable from S0001-S0017 GaN rows + S0009/S0011/S0014 competitors - no existing review provides it); repeatability statistics (S0218 protocol; S0068's 19,000-pulse stability as the field's high bar); bench calibration (S0051/S0148 templates); bandwidth derivation (S0076 characterization norm); field-unit presentation (needs calibration). The 'first quasi-helically symmetric stellarator' phrasing should be corrected to Garcia 2025's exact wording 'first and only stellarator experiment optimized for quasi-helical symmetry' (S0128); Garren & Boozer (S0124) show exact QHS is impossible in principle.",S0001;S0004;S0005;S0006;S0009;S0011;S0014;S0016;S0017;S0051;S0065;S0068;S0076;S0124;S0126;S0128;S0148;S0218,strong,"Stage 00 conflict C1 stands: parent-project '2023, published' framing is contradicted by the supplied 2026 submission/decline records; no published record of the manuscript was found in this stage's searches.",Figure-level reproduction of manuscript claims from raw HSX data was not attempted (Stage 00 checked file presence only).
6	Q5,Compare a revised Sensors Letters submission against arXiv preprint + substantially completed RSI study using the next HSX campaign (literature dimension),"Evidence only, decision deferred to stages 20/30. Genre analysis of the ledger: RSI is its most frequent venue (29/231) and routinely publishes deployment+calibration+validation instrumentation work (stellarator in-vessel probes S0154, Hall deployments S0143/S0173, system-integration-as-contribution S0226); FED/Nucl. Fusion carry the Hall-sensor qualification lineage (S0148, S0068, S0112); short device-letter venues reward device novelty - the axis Reviewer 2 attacked. The advisor group has RSI precedent (S0006).",S0006;S0068;S0093;S0112;S0143;S0148;S0154;S0173;S0226,moderate,none,"Preprints are excluded from the ledger by SOURCE_POLICY, so the arXiv half of the route comparison has no evidence base in this stage; venue decision requires the decline letter's resubmission terms (stage 30)."
7	Q6,"Specify the next experiment and analysis needed to close calibration, absolute-field, repeatability, uncertainty, bandwidth, conventional-probe-comparison, and novelty gaps (literature norms; plan itself is stage 40)","The fusion-instrumentation validation norm is established: itemized uncertainty budgets, calibration against an independent standard/model, accuracy vs a stated requirement, environmental qualification as a program, and multi-pulse stability. Sub-rows Q6A-Q6G give per-gap norms.",S0051;S0068;S0076;S0094;S0112;S0114;S0115;S0132;S0137;S0143;S0144;S0148;S0152;S0153;S0210;S0218;S0220,strong,none,What accuracy/bandwidth/drift constitutes success for a first-generation academic device is not established by any source - nearest bars are ITER/JET-grade and may be an unfair target.
8	Q6A,Absolute calibration and V_off closure,"Templates: traceable Hall-probe calibration with 5-term uncertainty budget (S0051); ITER OVSS campaign achieving ~2.5 mT calibration contribution against a 4 mT (2-sigma) requirement, 'at the limit of technical feasibility' (S0148); high-field Hall-coefficient fits with <0.11% error (S0115). Real-time attitude-independent bias estimation offers an in-situ algorithmic route (S0197).",S0051;S0115;S0148;S0197,strong,none,"Project 02's bench emulator shows an unresolved ~109x magnitude anomaly (supplied fact, conflict C6); no calibration coefficient exists for Tim's sensor."
9	Q6B,Absolute-field measurement in HSX,Precedent paradigm: CTH's GaAs Hall array validated against Biot-Savart vacuum-field predictions (S0143); W7-X flux-surface mapping as the stellarator gold standard (S0137); HSX's own V3FIT-optimized diagnostic study defines the reconstruction context a calibrated point-field sensor would feed (S0132).,S0132;S0137;S0143,strong,none,No HSX vacuum-field-vs-Hall-sensor comparison exists; requires a calibrated sensor plus HSX field model access.
10	Q6C,Repeatability / device-to-device statistics,"Norms: multi-geometry on-chip Hall-cell statistics (S0218); JET's 18-sensor +/-0.07% calibration stability over 19,000 pulses as the operational high bar (S0068); reproducibility-reporting agenda (S0221). AEIC explicitly requested repeatability across fabrication iterations (supplied fact C010).",S0068;S0218;S0221,strong,none,Only one module was tested per the decision letter; whether additional dies from the same run exist is NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SUPPLIED FILES.
11	Q6D,Uncertainty budget,Norms: EAST's itemized magnetics uncertainty budget (S0152); ITER Rogowski error modeling (S0094); GUM-vs-Monte-Carlo formal evaluation (S0220); Bayesian model-discrepancy separation (S0161); Allan-variance drift decomposition (S0168).,S0094;S0152;S0161;S0168;S0220,strong,none,none
12	Q6E,Bandwidth derivation and characterization,"Norm: swept characterization over the full band as in the 3-axis B-dot probe standard (10 kHz-50 MHz, S0076) and the RFX-mod2 digital chain (200 kHz, S0178); randomized-spinning readout preserving 2 MS/s Hall bandwidth shows the spinning/bandwidth trade-off is solvable (S0039). Reviewer 1 questioned the asserted 1 MHz figure (supplied fact C003).",S0039;S0076;S0178,strong,none,The manuscript's 1 MHz figure has no published derivation; a measured frequency-response curve for Tim's readout does not exist in supplied files.
13	Q6F,Conventional-probe (B-dot/Mirnov) comparison,"The AEIC-requested comparison has abundant reference literature (B-dot design/calibration S0076; Mirnov array practice S0072/S0075; drift-limitation contrast S0104/S0107) and a direct paradigm precedent (S0143). The literature's mature answer is hybrid coil+Hall fusion (S0118, S0122), which reframes the comparison as complementarity, not competition.",S0072;S0075;S0076;S0104;S0107;S0118;S0122;S0143,strong,none,No co-located Hall-vs-B-dot measurement exists in supplied HSX data; requires a campaign measurement (stage 40).
14	Q6G,Novelty-gap closure and claim wording,"The defensible claim: first GaN/AlGaN (WBG 2DEG) Hall sensor in-vessel in any confinement device and first Hall sensor of any kind in a QHS stellarator (absence finding, three independent lanes); NOT 'first fusion Hall diagnostic' (20-year non-GaN lineage S0066-S0070, S0112-S0122). Facility claim must match S0128's exact wording. First-deployment framing is publishable when rigor-documented (S0225-S0231 precedent class).",S0066;S0067;S0068;S0069;S0070;S0112;S0114;S0121;S0128;S0143;S0225;S0226;S0227;S0230,strong,Reviewer 1 vs Reviewer 2 novelty positions resolve at different claim granularities.,Absence-of-evidence basis; a global prior-art guarantee is impossible from a bounded search.
15	Q7,Screen concepts already supported by the supplied work for potentially protectable subject matter before public disclosure (research screen only),"Literature-side input to stage 50: prior art is dense for spinning-current/offset methods (S0033-S0043, 1990s origin), fusion Hall-probe deployment (S0066-S0070, S0111-S0122), hybrid coil+Hall Kalman fusion (S0118, S0122), and 3-axis Hall architectures (S0027, S0032, S0208). Any protectable scope would need to be narrower than these; no legal conclusion is drawn here.",S0027;S0032;S0033;S0038;S0041;S0066;S0068;S0112;S0114;S0118;S0122;S0208,moderate,none,Patent literature itself was not searched at this stage (SOURCE_POLICY excludes patents from this ledger); stage 50 owns the prior-art screen.
16	Q8,Produce a realistic 24-month PhD plan aligned with ~2-year graduation and startup preparation (literature dimension),"Literature-side input to stage 60: campaign-uncoupled work (calibration/uncertainty, fusion with existing data, reproducibility - S0051/S0158-S0180/S0218-S0221) can proceed regardless of HSX schedule; campaign-coupled work (probe comparison, vector probe, ML reconstruction training data - S0143/S0210/S0181) is schedule-bound; the ITER/JET qualification programs (S0114, S0068) show multi-year timescales for full qualification, implying scope discipline for a 24-month window.",S0051;S0068;S0114;S0143;S0181;S0210;S0218,moderate,none,HSX campaign schedule commitments are NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SUPPLIED FILES; timeline construction is stage 60.

1	# Research notes ΓÇö HSX Hall sensor readout
2	
3	Append new entries at the top (newest first). One dated section per entry.
4	Claude Code reads this file every session (see CLAUDE.md) so it always has
5	the current status without you re-explaining it.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 2026-07-08 ΓÇö first dynamic spinning run on the emulator (20 kHz, 20 mA)
10	Full session write-up: `journal/2026-07-08_spinning_emulator_20mA.md`.
11	- Config: 20 mA bias, 20 kHz spin, emulator = 4├ù680 ╬⌐ ring + 2.2 k╬⌐ across
12	  p1ΓÇôp2; R_G = 60.4 ╬⌐ (SMD "76X", confirmed) ΓåÆ gain 100.3; DSO-X 4022A,
13	  v_meas only (no sync). Data: `data/2026-07-08_test_spin.csv`.
14	- Γ£ô Clean 8-state staircase at 400 ┬╡s (muxes stepping correctly); raw
15	  pattern + ΓêÆ ΓêÆ + ΓêÆ + + ΓêÆ. **R9 = R10 = 2.0 V ΓåÆ leakage check PASSED**
16	  (20 mA reaches the bridge).
17	- Γ£ô **Offset cancellation works**: demod collapses the 686 mV raw offset
18	  to Γëñ 5 mV (ΓëÑ130├ù, limited by the scope's 8-bit quantization over 5
19	  cycles), reconstructing phase from f since sync wasn't captured.
20	- Γùæ **OPEN ANOMALY**: with 680 ╬⌐ + 2.2 k╬⌐ + 20 mA + gain 100.3 the output
21	  should rail (~75 V); measured a clean 0.686 V ΓÇö ~109├ù too small. R9=R10
22	  rules out leakage; R_G present rules out a missing gain resistor. Left:
23	  in-operation gain not ~100├ù, OR the 2.2 k╬⌐ not electrically unbalancing
24	  the bridge. **Resolve with the ╬öV gain check (plan ┬º4 Day 3ΓÇô4) next
25	  session ΓÇö top priority.** Don't calibrate to these magnitudes yet.
26	- New reusable tool: `analysis/spin_verify_nosync.py` (fold/demod/bridge-
27	  consistency when only v_meas was captured).
28	- Plan status (This Week ┬º4/┬º6.1): done ΓÇö logic bring-up, emulator+current
29	  source, R9/R10 leakage check, dynamic spin+demod cancellation. Not done ΓÇö
30	  ╬öV gain check, static 8-state survey, sync capture, noise floor PSD,
31	  f-sweep, rail-ripple spectrum. Full table in the journal.
32	
33	## 2026-07-08 ΓÇö MODE 1 low-frequency extension (delay cycles)
34	- Extended the spin firmware's phase-rate range downward. Each phase is
35	  now emitted as `CYCLES_PER_PHASE = 8` PIO cycles (a `[7]` delay on the
36	  `set`), so the SM runs at 8┬╖f. This decouples the phase rate from the
37	  PIO clock-divider floor: a single-cycle phase can't go below ~2.3 kHz
38	  at the Pico 2's 150 MHz sys clock (max divider 65536), but 8
39	  cycles/phase drops the floor to **~290 Hz** ΓÇö so f = 1 kHz now works.
40	  Verified 1k/5k/40k/100k land on clean divisors; <290 Hz is rejected
41	  with a clear message. `set_freq` reports the achieved *phase* rate.
42	- Applied to both `main.py` and `pico2_spin_scope.py` (kept consistent).
43	- Note: **5 kHz and above need no reflash** ΓÇö they were always above the
44	  floor; use `freq 5000` / `start 5000` on the existing firmware. The
45	  reflash only matters for sub-2.3 kHz rates. Recommended demod range
46	  (SPECS: 10kΓÇô100k for usable BW) is unchanged; the low end is for
47	  bench visualization. Remember to pass the matching `--f` to
48	  `hsx_demod_scope_csv.py`.
49	
50	## 2026-07-08 ΓÇö firmware split into two modes; second test setup defined
51	- Firmware reorganized into two self-contained mode files (same J3 pin
52	  map, same verified phase table): `firmware/pico2/pico2_spin_scope.py`
53	  (mode 1 ΓÇö full current-spinning, scope as DAQ, adds `survey()` and
54	  `scope_notes()`) and `firmware/pico2/pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py`
55	  (mode 2 ΓÇö muxes parked in states 2/3/6/7: external source biases
56	  p2 ΓåÆ p4, amp reads the p1/p3 difference, Pico ADC on GP26 ΓåÉ J4
57	  digitizes; 4-state chop cancels amplifier offset, plate offset o does
58	  NOT cancel ΓÇö single-axis physics). `pico2_hsx_phase_clock.py` kept as
59	  heritage, unchanged.
60	- `main.py` consolidated into a **self-contained single-file build**
61	  carrying both modes: set `MODE = 1` or `2` (and `DEFAULT_FREQ`) at the
62	  top, flash only that one file. Lights the onboard LED (alive
63	  indicator), then runs the selected mode's menu; live object exposed as
64	  `dev` for the REPL. Added a `predict`/`predict_offset` bridge-offset

# Research notes ΓÇö HSX Hall sensor readout

Append new entries at the top (newest first). One dated section per entry.
Claude Code reads this file every session (see CLAUDE.md) so it always has
the current status without you re-explaining it.

---

## 2026-07-08 ΓÇö first dynamic spinning run on the emulator (20 kHz, 20 mA)
Full session write-up: `journal/2026-07-08_spinning_emulator_20mA.md`.
- Config: 20 mA bias, 20 kHz spin, emulator = 4├ù680 ╬⌐ ring + 2.2 k╬⌐ across
  p1ΓÇôp2; R_G = 60.4 ╬⌐ (SMD "76X", confirmed) ΓåÆ gain 100.3; DSO-X 4022A,
  v_meas only (no sync). Data: `data/2026-07-08_test_spin.csv`.
- Γ£ô Clean 8-state staircase at 400 ┬╡s (muxes stepping correctly); raw
  pattern + ΓêÆ ΓêÆ + ΓêÆ + + ΓêÆ. **R9 = R10 = 2.0 V ΓåÆ leakage check PASSED**
  (20 mA reaches the bridge).
- Γ£ô **Offset cancellation works**: demod collapses the 686 mV raw offset
  to Γëñ 5 mV (ΓëÑ130├ù, limited by the scope's 8-bit quantization over 5
  cycles), reconstructing phase from f since sync wasn't captured.
- Γùæ **OPEN ANOMALY**: with 680 ╬⌐ + 2.2 k╬⌐ + 20 mA + gain 100.3 the output
  should rail (~75 V); measured a clean 0.686 V ΓÇö ~109├ù too small. R9=R10
  rules out leakage; R_G present rules out a missing gain resistor. Left:
  in-operation gain not ~100├ù, OR the 2.2 k╬⌐ not electrically unbalancing
  the bridge. **Resolve with the ╬öV gain check (plan ┬º4 Day 3ΓÇô4) next
  session ΓÇö top priority.** Don't calibrate to these magnitudes yet.
- New reusable tool: `analysis/spin_verify_nosync.py` (fold/demod/bridge-
  consistency when only v_meas was captured).
- Plan status (This Week ┬º4/┬º6.1): done ΓÇö logic bring-up, emulator+current
  source, R9/R10 leakage check, dynamic spin+demod cancellation. Not done ΓÇö
  ╬öV gain check, static 8-state survey, sync capture, noise floor PSD,
  f-sweep, rail-ripple spectrum. Full table in the journal.

## 2026-07-08 ΓÇö MODE 1 low-frequency extension (delay cycles)
- Extended the spin firmware's phase-rate range downward. Each phase is
  now emitted as `CYCLES_PER_PHASE = 8` PIO cycles (a `[7]` delay on the
  `set`), so the SM runs at 8┬╖f. This decouples the phase rate from the
  PIO clock-divider floor: a single-cycle phase can't go below ~2.3 kHz
  at the Pico 2's 150 MHz sys clock (max divider 65536), but 8
  cycles/phase drops the floor to **~290 Hz** ΓÇö so f = 1 kHz now works.
  Verified 1k/5k/40k/100k land on clean divisors; <290 Hz is rejected
  with a clear message. `set_freq` reports the achieved *phase* rate.
- Applied to both `main.py` and `pico2_spin_scope.py` (kept consistent).
- Note: **5 kHz and above need no reflash** ΓÇö they were always above the
  floor; use `freq 5000` / `start 5000` on the existing firmware. The
  reflash only matters for sub-2.3 kHz rates. Recommended demod range
  (SPECS: 10kΓÇô100k for usable BW) is unchanged; the low end is for
  bench visualization. Remember to pass the matching `--f` to
  `hsx_demod_scope_csv.py`.

## 2026-07-08 ΓÇö firmware split into two modes; second test setup defined
- Firmware reorganized into two self-contained mode files (same J3 pin
  map, same verified phase table): `firmware/pico2/pico2_spin_scope.py`
  (mode 1 ΓÇö full current-spinning, scope as DAQ, adds `survey()` and
  `scope_notes()`) and `firmware/pico2/pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py`
  (mode 2 ΓÇö muxes parked in states 2/3/6/7: external source biases
  p2 ΓåÆ p4, amp reads the p1/p3 difference, Pico ADC on GP26 ΓåÉ J4
  digitizes; 4-state chop cancels amplifier offset, plate offset o does
  NOT cancel ΓÇö single-axis physics). `pico2_hsx_phase_clock.py` kept as
  heritage, unchanged.
- `main.py` consolidated into a **self-contained single-file build**
  carrying both modes: set `MODE = 1` or `2` (and `DEFAULT_FREQ`) at the
  top, flash only that one file. Lights the onboard LED (alive
  indicator), then runs the selected mode's menu; live object exposed as
  `dev` for the REPL. Added a `predict`/`predict_offset` bridge-offset
  helper to mode 2 (o = I┬╖(R41┬╖R23 ΓêÆ R12┬╖R34)/╬úR ΓåÆ expected v_meas) for
  the emulator plug. The two module files remain as importable libraries
  (RSI 3-board work) mirroring the same logic. Smoke-tested both modes'
  boot paths with the Pico hardware stubbed.
- New doc `docs/second_test_setup_static_bias.md` ΓÇö the second test
  setup: purpose (health checks, gen-2 raw-offset incoming inspection,
  2023-style continuity, fast-mode fallback), wiring incl. ADC tap and
  optional level-shift network, expected numbers, ADC limits (unipolar,
  ~0.8 mV/LSB ΓÇö health-check grade only).
- Bring-up plan revised (Jul 8): Day-2/Day-3 firmware references, new
  ┬º6.3, fast-mode item ┬º2.8, Week-3 drift note, risk register.
- Reader-friendly HTML mirrors generated next to the plan docs
  (`.html` beside `.md`); regenerate whenever the markdown changes.
- No changes to any measured value, the phase table, or the demod sign
  convention.

## 2026-07-06 ΓÇö folder restructure
- Project now lives inside the reorganized `01/` tree with a
  root-level CLAUDE.md, shared `.claude/` automation (`/log`, `/specs`,

- Firmware moved to `firmware/pico2/` ΓÇö module unchanged, plus new

- Added `docs/SPECS.md`: one-page quick reference (phase table, pin maps,

- New sibling project `03_HSX_Vector_Probe_RSI2026/` created for the 2ΓÇô3

## 2026-07-06

1	# RSI 2026ΓÇô27: Calibrated vector Hall probe in HSX ΓÇö experiment & publication plan
2	
3	**Working title:** *A calibrated three-axis AlGaN/GaN Hall-effect probe
4	with spinning-current readout for in-vessel magnetic field measurements
5	in the HSX stellarator*
6	
7	**Target journal:** Review of Scientific Instruments (regular article).
8	**Target submission:** ~March 2027. **First author:** Y. Zhao.
9	**Revised:** July 8, 2026 ΓÇö incoming-inspection tooling settled: the
10	project-02 firmware now has a dedicated static-bias mode
11	(`../02_HSX_Hall_Sensor_Readout/firmware/pico2/pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py`,
12	setup doc `../02_.../docs/second_test_setup_static_bias.md`) that
13	measures the raw plate offset at 100 ┬╡A scope-free ΓÇö the ┬º2.1 batch
14	survey tool. Reader-friendly HTML versions of the plan docs now sit next
15	to their markdown.
16	
17	**Scope statement (fixed):** this campaign measures plasma and magnetic
18	fields inside HSX. No neutron or gamma irradiation experiments are
19	performed or claimed. Radiation response is covered by the co-authored
20	TCAD modeling manuscript (Van Gorp, Dawes, Zhao, Senesky, in prep.),
21	which is cited as complementary work; experimental radiation hardness
22	appears, at most, as one sentence of outlook.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 1. Where the trajectory stands, and the gap this paper fills
27	
28	The 2023 Sensors Letters paper established feasibility: a packaged
29	AlGaN/GaN Hall sensor survived 68 consecutive HSX shots in-vessel and
30	tracked plasma-dependent field dynamics in real time. Its own text
31	concedes the limits ΓÇö the sensor was voltage-biased with an uncalibrated
32	offset V_off, produced a single axis, and validated only by *temporal
33	correlation* with the diamagnetic loop. Its stated future work was
34	absolute calibration against HSX magnetic diagnostics, extended-duration
35	offset stability, and lower-noise readout.
36	
37	Project 02 (bench now, HSX install Aug 2026) already answers the
38	single-axis half of that list: 100 ┬╡A current bias, four-phase
39	spinning-current with polarity chopping (kills plate and amplifier
40	offsets by construction), AD8429 readout, and a traceable Helmholtz +
41	in-situ calibration path. What it does not do is measure a vector, and a
42	single scalar component is a weak instrument in a machine whose whole
43	identity is field *geometry* ΓÇö HSX is the first quasi-helically
44	symmetric stellarator, and its diagnostics literature (PfirschΓÇôSchl├╝ter
45	current measurements, equilibrium-reconstruction optimization) is about
46	field direction and structure, not just magnitude.
47	
48	The lab lineage also points at RSI specifically: the group's
49	high-temperature 2DEG sensitivity paper (Alpert et al. 2020) is an RSI
50	article, and the canonical fusion-magnetics instrument papers (e.g.
51	Strait's DIII-D magnetic diagnostic system) live there too. An
52	instrument paper ΓÇö *what was built, how it was calibrated, traceability,
53	quantified in-machine performance* ΓÇö is exactly RSI's format.
54	
55	**Thesis of the paper:** the first absolutely calibrated, multi-axis
56	(2ΓÇô3 component) GaN Hall-effect probe operated inside a stellarator,
57	with offset suppression by spinning-current demonstrated in-vessel, and
58	vector output validated quantitatively against the computed vacuum field
59	and HSX's standard diagnostics ΓÇö upgrading 2023's "temporal correlation"
60	to numbers with uncertainties.
61	
62	Contribution list (for the intro, and for reviewers):
63	1. Vector measurement: 2ΓÇô3 orthogonal AlGaN/GaN plates in one compact
64	   UHV-compatible ceramic cube package.
65	2. In-vessel spinning-current operation: offset-free readout at the
66	   probe, with measured long-sequence offset stability vs the 2023
67	   uncalibrated baseline.
68	3. Absolute calibration chain: bench Helmholtz (matrix calibration,
69	   traceable to geometry + 0.1 % shunt) anchored in situ by coil-only
70	   shots against the computed vacuum field at a surveyed probe pose.
71	4. Quantified plasma measurements: component-resolved ignition
72	   transients and discharge dynamics with an uncertainty budget.
73	
74	---
75	
76	## 2. Instrument
77	
78	### 2.1 Gen-2 sensor dies (larger bond pads)
79	
80	Pad enlargement doesn't move first-order sensitivity: S_I Γëê r_n┬╖G_H/(q┬╖n_s)
81	is set by the 2DEG sheet density and plate geometry, both unchanged. What
82	it plausibly improves is exactly what a cube package stresses ΓÇö wirebond
83	yield (especially on non-horizontal faces), bond placement tolerance, and
84	contact resistance (ΓåÆ lower 1/f contact noise and raw offset). What it
85	may quietly change is the terminal-to-terminal plate resistance and the
86	effective shape factor if the metal encroaches on the octagon.
87	
88	Incoming inspection per die, before any packaging (half a day for a
89	batch):
90	- Full 2-terminal resistance map across all pin pairs; compare against
91	  the 2023 signature (~650 ╬⌐ opposite-pair). **If R changed, update the
92	  emulator arm value (649 ╬⌐ today) and the bias-return loading factor
93	  (0.83 today) in `../02_.../docs/SPECS.md` ΓÇö the ┬▒26 mV emulator
94	  expectation moves with them.**
95	- 3-terminal contact-resistance estimate on a sample of pads.
96	- Raw offset distribution at 100 ┬╡A across the batch (pick matched dies
97	  for the cube). **Standard tool:** the second test setup from project
98	  02 ΓÇö static bias p2 ΓåÆ p4, sense p1/p3, Pico-ADC readout
99	  (`../02_.../firmware/pico2/pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py`; procedure and
100	  limits in `../02_.../docs/second_test_setup_static_bias.md`). One
101	  packaged die in the LCC breakout, `measure_chopped()` per die
102	  (amplifier offset cancels; at zero field the result *is* the raw
103	  plate offset), log the distribution.
104	- Spot-check S_I with the Helmholtz on one packaged sample; expect
105	  Γëê 60 V/A/T unchanged.
106	
107	### 2.2 Cube module
108	
109	Concept: the proven single-die process ΓÇö die ΓåÆ LCC (Spectrum), Al wedge
110	bonds, EPO-TEK 353ND encapsulation, 150 ┬░C vacuum bake ΓÇö repeated per
111	face on a machinable ceramic (or zirconia, matching the 2023 holder)
112	cube, LCCs on 2 or 3 mutually orthogonal faces. Nothing new is qualified
113	except the cube itself and the face-mount adhesive/bake compatibility.
114	
115	Design points to settle in September:
116	- Cube size: set by LCC footprint + routing clearance; keep the probe
117	  head compact enough for the existing standoff/graphite-shield concept
118	  (shield likely needs a resize, not a redesign).
119	- Face flatness/orthogonality spec: the calibration matrix absorbs
120	  fixed misalignment, so ┬▒1┬░ machining is acceptable ΓÇö but it must be
121	  *stable* through bake and thermal cycling.
122	- Bond accessibility on vertical faces: this is the yield risk the
123	  larger pads exist to mitigate. Plan a mechanical-sample bond trial
124	  before committing flight dies.
125	- 2 vs 3 axes: build for 3; if bond yield or feedthrough pins force it,
126	  a 2-axis module is still a publishable vector instrument (state the
127	  choice honestly in the paper).
128	
129	### 2.3 Readout: replicate the 02 board per axis
130	
131	Decision: **three copies of `hsx_2026_v1`** rather than a new
132	multi-channel board rev. Rationale: the gerber/order package already
133	exists (`../02_.../circuit/hsx_setup_v1_Y23.zip`, hand-assembly ΓÇö budget
134	real bench days for two more builds), the design will have a full
135	bring-up campaign of heritage by September, and channel isolation comes
136	free (independent amps, independent floating supplies). A rev-B
137	3-channel board is strictly nicer and strictly riskier before a travel
138	date; park it as future work.
139	
140	Firmware: the project-02 Pico 2 firmware is already organized as two
141	mode files ΓÇö `pico2_spin_scope.py` (spinning, scope DAQ; the campaign
142	workhorse) and `pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py` (static bias, Pico-ADC
143	readout; incoming inspection and scope-free health checks at HSX). Both
144	carry over unchanged ΓÇö the fan-out below is electrical, not software.
145	
146	Synchronization: **one Pico 2 fans out the shared a0/a1/a2/EN** to all
147	three boards (each line drives three CMOS mux inputs ΓÇö trivial load).
148	All axes spin in phase, so one sync line (GP19) timestamps all three
149	demods and inter-axis phase skew is zero by construction. Grounds: each
150	board's GND1 commons at the scope via its SMA shield; bond the Pico
151	ground once, star-style, and verify no inter-board loop before the
152	trip.
153	
154	Bias: one floating ~100 ┬╡A source **per board** (REF200-style or the
155	battery box used in bring-up); do not share a source across plates ΓÇö
156	the spinning muxes would fight over it.
157	
158	### 2.4 Harness and feedthrough (open item #1 ΓÇö ask UW early)
159	
160	Three plates ├ù 4 wires = **12 signal conductors** (plus shields). The
161	2023 single-axis harness used 4 pins of a DSUB-9. Options: one DB-15
162	(12 + spares/shield) or two DSUB-9s. **Action, July:** email Wayne/
163	Thomas for the available feedthrough pin count and connector type on the
164	intended port; this decides the harness build and possibly the 2-vs-3
165	axis question. Keep per-plate pairs twisted; keep the 2023 pin
166	convention (bias pair / sense pair) per plate so the boards drop on.
167	
168	### 2.5 DAQ and the scope-memory question (open item #2)
169	
170	The DSOX1204G's four channels map perfectly: CH1ΓÇô3 = v_x, v_y, v_z,
171	CH4 = sync. Memory does not map perfectly: ~2 Mpts shared ΓåÆ ~500 kpts
172	per channel with all four on. The demod wants ΓëÑ ~10 samples per 25 ┬╡s
173	phase (f = 40 kHz), i.e. ΓëÑ ~0.4ΓÇô1 MSa/s. So per shot, pick one:
174	
175	| Strategy | Settings | Covers | Cost |
176	|---|---|---|---|
177	| A. Ignition window | 1 MSa/s, ~300ΓÇô500 ms capture, trigger near ECRH | breakdown + discharge, misses coil ramp | none ΓÇö default |
178	| B. Full shot, slower spin | f = 10ΓÇô20 kHz, 250ΓÇô400 kSa/s, ~1.2 s | whole shot incl. ramp | demod BW drops to ~0.3ΓÇô0.5 kHz |
179	| C. HSX DAQ channels | demod offline from their record | whole shot, their timebase | integration effort + their sampling limits |
180	
181	Run A as the workhorse, B for a few dedicated ramp-study shots, and
182	pursue C opportunistically ΓÇö it also solves the ~30 ms trigger-offset
183	annoyance from 2023 by putting everything on one clock. Decide by
184	end of October bench work.
185	
186	---
187	
188	## 3. Calibration plan (the heart of the paper)
189	
190	### 3.1 Per-axis scalar calibration
191	Reuse the project-02 Week-3 protocol per channel: bipolar Helmholtz
192	sweeps (┬▒2.7 mT), sensitivity-vs-bias linearity at 50/100/200/500 ┬╡A,
193	AC response 10 HzΓÇô3 kHz, hotplate 25ΓÇô100 ┬░C coefficient, overnight
194	drift. Targets unchanged: ~2 % absolute, < 0.5 % linearity.
195	
196	### 3.2 Vector (matrix) calibration
197	Model: **v = M┬╖B + b**, with v the three demodulated outputs, M a 3├ù3
198	matrix (per-axis gains on the diagonal, misalignment + cross-sensitivity
199	off-diagonal), b residual offsets (should be ~0 with spinning ΓÇö measure
200	it anyway; it's a headline number).
201	
202	Method: single-axis Helmholtz + a 3D-printed indexing cradle that holds
203	the cube in each of the six ┬▒face orientations (90┬░ indexed) plus two
204	45┬░ checks. At each orientation, sweep B over ┬▒2.5 mT and record all
205	three channels. Least-squares fit of M and b (24+ sweep-orientation
206	combinations, 12 unknowns ΓÇö well over-determined; report residuals).
207	Extract and report the misalignment angles from the polar decomposition
208	of M ΓÇö expect ~1ΓÇô2┬░ from assembly. Checks: planar-Hall cross-talk (drive
209	B in-plane of each die, confirm second-order), per-die temperature
210	coefficient (cube on hotplate), repeatability after a thermal cycle and
211	after re-mounting in the cradle.
212	
213	### 3.3 In-situ absolute anchor (the RSI centerpiece)
214	HSX coil-only shots produce a vacuum field that is *computable* at any
215	point from the coil currents and geometry. With the probe pose (position
216	+ orientation) surveyed on its mount, the predicted vector **B_vac** at
217	the probe is compared against **MΓü╗┬╣(v ΓêÆ b)** ΓÇö a quantitative,
218	component-by-component absolute check inside the machine, at multiple
219	field settings. This single figure upgrades the 2023 paper's
220	correlation-only validation into calibration traceability, and it is
221	what makes the paper an instruments paper rather than a demo. Requires:
222	(a) surveyed mount pose (photogrammetry or fixture CAD + machinist
223	survey; ┬▒1 mm, ┬▒0.5ΓÇô1┬░ is enough for a ~2 % / ~2┬░ budget), (b) UW's
224	vacuum-field computation at that pose for the requested settings ΓÇö both
225	go in the July email.
226	
227	### 3.4 Uncertainty budget (drafted now, filled by data)
228	
229	| Term | Expected size | Comes from |
230	|---|---|---|
231	| Helmholtz field constant | ~1 % | geometry + 0.1 % shunt, pickup-coil cross-check |
232	| Matrix fit residuals | < 0.5 % | ┬º3.2 fit |
233	| Pose survey ΓåÆ predicted B_vac | ~1 % / ~1┬░ | ┬º3.3 survey |
234	| Temperature coefficient over shot | small; measured | hotplate data + in-vessel ╬öT |
235	| Noise per axis | 25ΓÇô30 ┬╡T rms @ 1 kHz ENBW | bench PSD, re-verified in-vessel |
236	| **Total (goal)** | **Γëñ 2ΓÇô3 % magnitude, Γëñ 2┬░ direction** | |
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 4. HSX campaign #2 (target November 2026)
241	
242	Objectives, in priority order:
243	1. **Coil-only absolute validation** at 2ΓÇô3 field settings, repeated ΓÇö
244	   the ┬º3.3 anchor. This is the must-have; everything else is upside.
245	2. **Vector plasma dynamics:** component-resolved ignition transient and

# RSI 2026ΓÇô27: Calibrated vector Hall probe in HSX ΓÇö experiment & publication plan

**Working title:** *A calibrated three-axis AlGaN/GaN Hall-effect probe
with spinning-current readout for in-vessel magnetic field measurements
in the HSX stellarator*

**Target journal:** Review of Scientific Instruments (regular article).
**Target submission:** ~March 2027. **First author:** Y. Zhao.
**Revised:** July 8, 2026 ΓÇö incoming-inspection tooling settled: the
project-02 firmware now has a dedicated static-bias mode
(`../02_HSX_Hall_Sensor_Readout/firmware/pico2/pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py`,
setup doc `../02_.../docs/second_test_setup_static_bias.md`) that
measures the raw plate offset at 100 ┬╡A scope-free ΓÇö the ┬º2.1 batch
survey tool. Reader-friendly HTML versions of the plan docs now sit next
to their markdown.

**Scope statement (fixed):** this campaign measures plasma and magnetic
fields inside HSX. No neutron or gamma irradiation experiments are
performed or claimed. Radiation response is covered by the co-authored
TCAD modeling manuscript (Van Gorp, Dawes, Zhao, Senesky, in prep.),
which is cited as complementary work; experimental radiation hardness
appears, at most, as one sentence of outlook.

---

## 1. Where the trajectory stands, and the gap this paper fills

The 2023 Sensors Letters paper established feasibility: a packaged
AlGaN/GaN Hall sensor survived 68 consecutive HSX shots in-vessel and
tracked plasma-dependent field dynamics in real time. Its own text
concedes the limits ΓÇö the sensor was voltage-biased with an uncalibrated
offset V_off, produced a single axis, and validated only by *temporal
correlation* with the diamagnetic loop. Its stated future work was
absolute calibration against HSX magnetic diagnostics, extended-duration
offset stability, and lower-noise readout.

Project 02 (bench now, HSX install Aug 2026) already answers the
single-axis half of that list: 100 ┬╡A current bias, four-phase
spinning-current with polarity chopping (kills plate and amplifier
offsets by construction), AD8429 readout, and a traceable Helmholtz +
in-situ calibration path. What it does not do is measure a vector, and a
single scalar component is a weak instrument in a machine whose whole
identity is field *geometry* ΓÇö HSX is the first quasi-helically
symmetric stellarator, and its diagnostics literature (PfirschΓÇôSchl├╝ter
current measurements, equilibrium-reconstruction optimization) is about
field direction and structure, not just magnitude.

The lab lineage also points at RSI specifically: the group's
high-temperature 2DEG sensitivity paper (Alpert et al. 2020) is an RSI
article, and the canonical fusion-magnetics instrument papers (e.g.
Strait's DIII-D magnetic diagnostic system) live there too. An
instrument paper ΓÇö *what was built, how it was calibrated, traceability,
quantified in-machine performance* ΓÇö is exactly RSI's format.

**Thesis of the paper:** the first absolutely calibrated, multi-axis
(2ΓÇô3 component) GaN Hall-effect probe operated inside a stellarator,
with offset suppression by spinning-current demonstrated in-vessel, and
vector output validated quantitatively against the computed vacuum field
and HSX's standard diagnostics ΓÇö upgrading 2023's "temporal correlation"
to numbers with uncertainties.

Contribution list (for the intro, and for reviewers):
1. Vector measurement: 2ΓÇô3 orthogonal AlGaN/GaN plates in one compact
   UHV-compatible ceramic cube package.
2. In-vessel spinning-current operation: offset-free readout at the
   probe, with measured long-sequence offset stability vs the 2023
   uncalibrated baseline.
3. Absolute calibration chain: bench Helmholtz (matrix calibration,
   traceable to geometry + 0.1 % shunt) anchored in situ by coil-only
   shots against the computed vacuum field at a surveyed probe pose.
4. Quantified plasma measurements: component-resolved ignition
   transients and discharge dynamics with an uncertainty budget.

---

## 2. Instrument

### 2.1 Gen-2 sensor dies (larger bond pads)

Pad enlargement doesn't move first-order sensitivity: S_I Γëê r_n┬╖G_H/(q┬╖n_s)
is set by the 2DEG sheet density and plate geometry, both unchanged. What
it plausibly improves is exactly what a cube package stresses ΓÇö wirebond
yield (especially on non-horizontal faces), bond placement tolerance, and
contact resistance (ΓåÆ lower 1/f contact noise and raw offset). What it
may quietly change is the terminal-to-terminal plate resistance and the
effective shape factor if the metal encroaches on the octagon.

Incoming inspection per die, before any packaging (half a day for a
batch):
- Full 2-terminal resistance map across all pin pairs; compare against
  the 2023 signature (~650 ╬⌐ opposite-pair). **If R changed, update the
  emulator arm value (649 ╬⌐ today) and the bias-return loading factor
  (0.83 today) in `../02_.../docs/SPECS.md` ΓÇö the ┬▒26 mV emulator
  expectation moves with them.**
- 3-terminal contact-resistance estimate on a sample of pads.
- Raw offset distribution at 100 ┬╡A across the batch (pick matched dies
  for the cube). **Standard tool:** the second test setup from project
  02 ΓÇö static bias p2 ΓåÆ p4, sense p1/p3, Pico-ADC readout
  (`../02_.../firmware/pico2/pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py`; procedure and
  limits in `../02_.../docs/second_test_setup_static_bias.md`). One
  packaged die in the LCC breakout, `measure_chopped()` per die
  (amplifier offset cancels; at zero field the result *is* the raw
  plate offset), log the distribution.
- Spot-check S_I with the Helmholtz on one packaged sample; expect
  Γëê 60 V/A/T unchanged.

### 2.2 Cube module

Concept: the proven single-die process ΓÇö die ΓåÆ LCC (Spectrum), Al wedge
bonds, EPO-TEK 353ND encapsulation, 150 ┬░C vacuum bake ΓÇö repeated per
face on a machinable ceramic (or zirconia, matching the 2023 holder)
cube, LCCs on 2 or 3 mutually orthogonal faces. Nothing new is qualified
except the cube itself and the face-mount adhesive/bake compatibility.

Design points to settle in September:
- Cube size: set by LCC footprint + routing clearance; keep the probe
  head compact enough for the existing standoff/graphite-shield concept
  (shield likely needs a resize, not a redesign).
- Face flatness/orthogonality spec: the calibration matrix absorbs
  fixed misalignment, so ┬▒1┬░ machining is acceptable ΓÇö but it must be
  *stable* through bake and thermal cycling.
- Bond accessibility on vertical faces: this is the yield risk the
  larger pads exist to mitigate. Plan a mechanical-sample bond trial
  before committing flight dies.
- 2 vs 3 axes: build for 3; if bond yield or feedthrough pins force it,
  a 2-axis module is still a publishable vector instrument (state the
  choice honestly in the paper).

### 2.3 Readout: replicate the 02 board per axis

Decision: **three copies of `hsx_2026_v1`** rather than a new
multi-channel board rev. Rationale: the gerber/order package already
exists (`../02_.../circuit/hsx_setup_v1_Y23.zip`, hand-assembly ΓÇö budget
real bench days for two more builds), the design will have a full
bring-up campaign of heritage by September, and channel isolation comes
free (independent amps, independent floating supplies). A rev-B
3-channel board is strictly nicer and strictly riskier before a travel
date; park it as future work.

Firmware: the project-02 Pico 2 firmware is already organized as two
mode files ΓÇö `pico2_spin_scope.py` (spinning, scope DAQ; the campaign
workhorse) and `pico2_static_bias_p2p4.py` (static bias, Pico-ADC
readout; incoming inspection and scope-free health checks at HSX). Both
carry over unchanged ΓÇö the fan-out below is electrical, not software.

Synchronization: **one Pico 2 fans out the shared a0/a1/a2/EN** to all
three boards (each line drives three CMOS mux inputs ΓÇö trivial load).
All axes spin in phase, so one sync line (GP19) timestamps all three
demods and inter-axis phase skew is zero by construction. Grounds: each
board's GND1 commons at the scope via its SMA shield; bond the Pico
ground once, star-style, and verify no inter-board loop before the
trip.

Bias: one floating ~100 ┬╡A source **per board** (REF200-style or the
battery box used in bring-up); do not share a source across plates ΓÇö
the spinning muxes would fight over it.

### 2.4 Harness and feedthrough (open item #1 ΓÇö ask UW early)

Three plates ├ù 4 wires = **12 signal conductors** (plus shields). The
2023 single-axis harness used 4 pins of a DSUB-9. Options: one DB-15
(12 + spares/shield) or two DSUB-9s. **Action, July:** email Wayne/
Thomas for the available feedthrough pin count and connector type on the
intended port; this decides the harness build and possibly the 2-vs-3
axis question. Keep per-plate pairs twisted; keep the 2023 pin
convention (bias pair / sense pair) per plate so the boards drop on.

### 2.5 DAQ and the scope-memory question (open item #2)

The DSOX1204G's four channels map perfectly: CH1ΓÇô3 = v_x, v_y, v_z,
CH4 = sync. Memory does not map perfectly: ~2 Mpts shared ΓåÆ ~500 kpts
per channel with all four on. The demod wants ΓëÑ ~10 samples per 25 ┬╡s
phase (f = 40 kHz), i.e. ΓëÑ ~0.4ΓÇô1 MSa/s. So per shot, pick one:

| Strategy | Settings | Covers | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Ignition window | 1 MSa/s, ~300ΓÇô500 ms capture, trigger near ECRH | breakdown + discharge, misses coil ramp | none ΓÇö default |
| B. Full shot, slower spin | f = 10ΓÇô20 kHz, 250ΓÇô400 kSa/s, ~1.2 s | whole shot incl. ramp | demod BW drops to ~0.3ΓÇô0.5 kHz |
| C. HSX DAQ channels | demod offline from their record | whole shot, their timebase | integration effort + their sampling limits |

Run A as the workhorse, B for a few dedicated ramp-study shots, and
pursue C opportunistically ΓÇö it also solves the ~30 ms trigger-offset
annoyance from 2023 by putting everything on one clock. Decide by
end of October bench work.

---

## 3. Calibration plan (the heart of the paper)

### 3.1 Per-axis scalar calibration
Reuse the project-02 Week-3 protocol per channel: bipolar Helmholtz
sweeps (┬▒2.7 mT), sensitivity-vs-bias linearity at 50/100/200/500 ┬╡A,
AC response 10 HzΓÇô3 kHz, hotplate 25ΓÇô100 ┬░C coefficient, overnight
drift. Targets unchanged: ~2 % absolute, < 0.5 % linearity.

### 3.2 Vector (matrix) calibration
Model: **v = M┬╖B + b**, with v the three demodulated outputs, M a 3├ù3
matrix (per-axis gains on the diagonal, misalignment + cross-sensitivity
off-diagonal), b residual offsets (should be ~0 with spinning ΓÇö measure
it anyway; it's a headline number).

Method: single-axis Helmholtz + a 3D-printed indexing cradle that holds
the cube in each of the six ┬▒face orientations (90┬░ indexed) plus two
45┬░ checks. At each orientation, sweep B over ┬▒2.5 mT and record all
three channels. Least-squares fit of M and b (24+ sweep-orientation
combinations, 12 unknowns ΓÇö well over-determined; report residuals).
Extract and report the misalignment angles from the polar decomposition
of M ΓÇö expect ~1ΓÇô2┬░ from assembly. Checks: planar-Hall cross-talk (drive
B in-plane of each die, confirm second-order), per-die temperature
coefficient (cube on hotplate), repeatability after a thermal cycle and
after re-mounting in the cradle.

### 3.3 In-situ absolute anchor (the RSI centerpiece)
HSX coil-only shots produce a vacuum field that is *computable* at any
point from the coil currents and geometry. With the probe pose (position
+ orientation) surveyed on its mount, the predicted vector **B_vac** at
the probe is compared against **MΓü╗┬╣(v ΓêÆ b)** ΓÇö a quantitative,
component-by-component absolute check inside the machine, at multiple
field settings. This single figure upgrades the 2023 paper's
correlation-only validation into calibration traceability, and it is
what makes the paper an instruments paper rather than a demo. Requires:
(a) surveyed mount pose (photogrammetry or fixture CAD + machinist
survey; ┬▒1 mm, ┬▒0.5ΓÇô1┬░ is enough for a ~2 % / ~2┬░ budget), (b) UW's
vacuum-field computation at that pose for the requested settings ΓÇö both
go in the July email.

### 3.4 Uncertainty budget (drafted now, filled by data)

| Term | Expected size | Comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Helmholtz field constant | ~1 % | geometry + 0.1 % shunt, pickup-coil cross-check |
| Matrix fit residuals | < 0.5 % | ┬º3.2 fit |
| Pose survey ΓåÆ predicted B_vac | ~1 % / ~1┬░ | ┬º3.3 survey |
| Temperature coefficient over shot | small; measured | hotplate data + in-vessel ╬öT |
| Noise per axis | 25ΓÇô30 ┬╡T rms @ 1 kHz ENBW | bench PSD, re-verified in-vessel |
| **Total (goal)** | **Γëñ 2ΓÇô3 % magnitude, Γëñ 2┬░ direction** | |

---

## 4. HSX campaign #2 (target November 2026)

Objectives, in priority order:
1. **Coil-only absolute validation** at 2ΓÇô3 field settings, repeated ΓÇö
   the ┬º3.3 anchor. This is the must-have; everything else is upside.
2. **Vector plasma dynamics:** component-resolved ignition transient and
   discharge fluctuations across the same discharge taxonomy as 2023
   (high-energy / late-breakdown / failed-breakdown) for continuity.
3. **Offset stability, spinning on:** a long repeated-shot sequence (and
   idle dwell between shots) tracking b(t) ΓÇö the direct, quantified
   answer to 2023's V_off problem.
4. Opportunistic: compare measured field direction against
   equilibrium-reconstruction expectations (Chlechowitz-style) with the
   UW team ΓÇö a physics hook, and co-author engagement.

Shot-list request to Wayne/Thomas (send with the July email):

| Ask | Shots | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Coil-only, setting 1/2/3, ├ù3 each | ~9 | absolute anchor + repeatability |

| Mount survey + vacuum-field calc at pose | ΓÇö | ┬º3.3 |
| Trigger/clock tie-in or offset characterization | ΓÇö | fix the ~30 ms DAQ offset |

Plus a shot-replay rehearsal at Stanford in October (wavegen playback of
2023 traces through the full 3-channel chain, long cable, EMI checks) so
the trip burns zero shots on debugging ΓÇö same philosophy as the Week-4
rehearsal in the 02 plan.

---

## 5. Paper skeleton and figure plan

Skeleton (RSI conventions): I. Introduction (fusion magnetics drift
problem ΓåÆ Hall alternative ΓåÆ GaN for in-vessel ΓåÆ 2023 demo and its
gaps ΓåÆ this instrument). II. Probe design (dies, cube package,
harness). III. Readout (spinning-current theory recap, per-axis boards,
synchronization, DAQ). IV. Calibration (scalar, matrix, in-situ anchor,
uncertainty budget). V. HSX results (coil-only validation, vector
plasma dynamics, offset stability). VI. Discussion & outlook (rev-B
integrated multichannel readout; radiation response per the co-authored
TCAD modeling ΓÇö cited, not performed). VII. Conclusion.

| Fig. | Content |

| 1 | Cube module: photo + exploded schematic, die/LCC/faces, in-vessel mount |
| 2 | 3-channel readout architecture with shared clock fan-out + timing diagram |
| 3 | Matrix calibration: orientation sweeps, fitted M, residuals; misalignment angles |

# 02 ΓÇö Research-direction decision (Stage 20)

**Basis:** the validated Stage 10D evidence package
([`01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv`](01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv), 231 verified peer-reviewed
sources S0001ΓÇôS0231; [`01_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md`](01_LITERATURE_REVIEW.md);
[`01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv`](01_EVIDENCE_MAP.csv)), the Stage 00 baselines
([`00_CLAIM_BASELINE.csv`](00_CLAIM_BASELINE.csv) claims C001ΓÇôC025;
[`00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md`](00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md) conflicts C1ΓÇôC6), the
supplied decision letter
([`../inputs/Decision_Letter_IEEE_2026-07-23.pdf`](../inputs/Decision_Letter_IEEE_2026-07-23.pdf)),
and direct re-reads of the parent bench truth
([`../../02_HSX_Hall_Sensor_Readout/NOTES.md`](../../02_HSX_Hall_Sensor_Readout/NOTES.md))
and the vector-probe plan
([`../../03_HSX_Vector_Probe_RSI2026/docs/rsi_experiment_and_publication_plan.md`](../../03_HSX_Vector_Probe_RSI2026/docs/rsi_experiment_and_publication_plan.md)).
Citations use `[S####]` with a `https://doi.org/...` link on first use.
Supplied project facts cite the file, not a ledger ID. Epistemic labels:
*Supplied fact*, *External evidence*, *Inference*, *Recommendation*,
*Proposed experiment*, *Unresolved gate*.

**Standing corrections this decision honors:** the manuscript is
**unpublished** ΓÇö submitted 2-Jul-2026, declined 23-Jul-2026 with an
invitation to revise and resubmit (conflict C1; claims C011/C012). The
parent memory's "2023, published" framing is unsupported and is not relied
on anywhere below. Project 02's "calibrated" language is **aspirational**
(conflict C6): the demonstrated result is ΓëÑ130├ù offset cancellation on a
resistor-ring emulator with an open ~109├ù magnitude anomaly (claims
C016/C017). Tim currently has, per supplied evidence, **zero accepted
first-author publications** ΓÇö which materially shapes the risk posture of
this decision.

---

## 1. Executive verdict

**CONTINUE the GaN Hall magnetic-diagnostics direction, with a substantial
adjustment in where the novelty is claimed and how the output portfolio is
structured. Decision class: ADJUST (option OPT2). Do not change direction.**

Three findings force each part of that verdict:

1. **The direction is publishable ΓÇö at a specific claim granularity.**
   Across three independent literature lanes, no peer-reviewed GaN/AlGaN
   Hall sensor was found deployed inside any tokamak or stellarator, and no
   Hall sensor of any kind was found in a quasi-helically symmetric
   stellarator (absence finding; bounded search). Meanwhile, Hall sensing is
   the fusion field's own chosen answer to the integrator-drift problem ΓÇö
   JET's InSb probes ran 11+ years at ┬▒0.07% stability
   [S0068](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/ac8aad), and ITER's
   steady-state magnetic diagnostic is a 60-unit bismuth Hall array
   [S0113](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4732077),
   [S0114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5038871). The concept is validated by
   the field; the specific material-plus-facility combination is unclaimed.

2. **Continuing *as currently framed* would fail again.** Reviewer 2's
   novelty objection is the literature's own verdict on device-granularity
   claims: GaN Hall device physics, spinning-current offset cancellation,
   and temperature behavior are already published ΓÇö largely by the
   advisor's own group [S0004](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2019.2895546),
   [S0005](https://doi.org/10.1109/LSENS.2019.2898157),
   [S0006](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5139911),
   [S0012](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0305414), and spinning-current dates
   to 1990 [S0033](https://doi.org/10.1016/0924-4247%2889%2980069-X). The
   adjustment is to *cite that record as prior art and claim the
   application, the finished calibrated measurement, and the measurement
   architecture* ΓÇö the granularity at which Reviewer 1 ("novel and unique")
   and the first-deployment publication precedent class
   [S0226](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0095907),
   [S0227](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11214-025-01170-w),
   [S0230](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40517-021-00204-0) operate.

3. **A genuine change of direction is dominated.** The best-supported
   change option (software-only stellarator-magnetics methods, ┬º3.3) scores
   below both continuation variants: it abandons the single asset no
   competitor has (a survived, shot-resolved in-vessel GaN deployment,
   claims C001/C002), sits poorly with the advisor group's device
   identity, and depends on an HSX training-scale database whose existence
   is NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SUPPLIED FILES. It is retained as the named
   fallback (┬º8), not the plan.

The adjusted continuation (OPT2) keeps the **finished, absolutely
calibrated sensing output as the non-negotiable centerpiece** ΓÇö exactly
what the decline letter demands (claim C010) ΓÇö and layers on
campaign-uncoupled, software-heavy work packages (comparison table,
multi-die repeatability, formal uncertainty budget, hybrid Hall+inductive
drift fusion) so that no single paper depends on both HSX campaigns
happening on schedule. It is also, verbatim, the user's own original
research interest: GaN Hall diagnostics *"with or without conventional
coils sensors, together, to resolve the drift problem"*
([`../inputs/ORIGINAL_REQUEST.txt`](../inputs/ORIGINAL_REQUEST.txt)) ΓÇö the
original interest was never device novelty; the first manuscript simply
claimed the wrong axis.

---

## 2. Scoring method: scale, weights, calculations, uncertainty, sensitivity

### 2.1 Scale and beneficial-direction convention

Every criterion is scored **1ΓÇô5, where 5 is always better for Tim**. For
the two burden columns and the risk column this means the scale is
inverted relative to the raw quantity: `cleanroom_burden = 5` means
*lowest* cleanroom burden, `experimental_burden = 5` means *lightest*
experimental load, `schedule_risk = 5` means *lowest* schedule risk. This
is the beneficial-direction convention required by the stage prompt, and
the CSV cells in [`02_DIRECTION_SCORECARD.csv`](02_DIRECTION_SCORECARD.csv)
follow it.

### 2.2 Weights (baseline W_A) and their rationale

Weights are anchored to MISSION.md's fixed preferences (Γëê2-year
graduation, low cleanroom, novelty in application/software, startup 2029/30
preparation) ΓÇö not chosen to favor a predetermined winner.

| Criterion | Weight | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| 24_month_publishability | 0.20 | Graduation in ~2 years with currently zero accepted first-author papers makes this the binding constraint |
| novelty_strength | 0.15 | The decline was a novelty decline; the next submission cannot lose on this axis again |
| evidence_strength | 0.10 | How much of the option already stands on demonstrated results (claims C001ΓÇôC023) |
| cleanroom_burden (5=low) | 0.10 | Explicit user constraint |
| experimental_burden (5=low) | 0.08 | Time-cost of bench/campaign work against the 24-month clock |
| software_simulation_leverage | 0.10 | Explicit user preference for novelty via software/simulation |
| advisor_group_fit | 0.12 | The thesis must be defensible in the Senesky group; misfit is a structural risk |
| startup_optionality | 0.07 | Real but subordinate to graduating |
| schedule_risk (5=low) | 0.08 | Exposure to events Tim does not control (HSX schedule, die supply) |
| **Sum** | **1.00** | |

### 2.3 Scores and calculations

Weighted score = ╬ú (weight ├ù score). Per-cell justifications are in
┬º3ΓÇô┬º5; the arithmetic:

| Criterion (weight) | OPT1 | OPT2 | OPT3 | OPT4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 24_month_publishability (0.20) | 4 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| novelty_strength (0.15) | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| evidence_strength (0.10) | 4 | 4 | 2 | 3 |
| cleanroom_burden (0.10) | 3 | 4 | 5 | 1 |
| experimental_burden (0.08) | 2 | 3 | 5 | 2 |
| software_simulation_leverage (0.10) | 3 | 5 | 5 | 2 |
| advisor_group_fit (0.12) | 5 | 4 | 2 | 5 |
| startup_optionality (0.07) | 4 | 5 | 3 | 3 |
| schedule_risk (0.08) | 2 | 4 | 3 | 2 |
| **Weighted score** | **3.45** | **4.29** | **3.34** | **2.58** |
| **Rank** | 2 | **1** | 3 | 4 |

Worked example (OPT2): 0.20┬╖5 + 0.15┬╖4 + 0.10┬╖4 + 0.10┬╖4 + 0.08┬╖3 +
0.10┬╖5 + 0.12┬╖4 + 0.07┬╖5 + 0.08┬╖4 = 1.00 + 0.60 + 0.40 + 0.40 + 0.24 +
0.50 + 0.48 + 0.35 + 0.32 = **4.29**.

### 2.4 Uncertainty

Cell scores are ordinal expert judgments grounded in cited evidence, with
a realistic uncertainty of ┬▒1 point per cell. Propagating ┬▒1 independent
per-cell uncertainty through the weights gives a 1╧â weighted-score
uncertainty of ΓêÜ(╬úwß╡ó┬▓) Γëê **┬▒0.35**, and Γëê ┬▒0.50 for the *difference*
between two options. Consequences:

- **OPT2's margin over OPT1 (0.84) is robust** (~1.7├ù the difference
  uncertainty). The #1 rank is stable.
- **The OPT1-vs-OPT3 gap (0.11) is a statistical tie.** The ordering of
  ranks 2 and 3 should not be treated as meaningful; what is meaningful is
  that both trail OPT2 by ΓëÑ0.8.
- OPT4's last place is robust (gap ΓëÑ 0.76 to every other option).

### 2.5 Sensitivity to plausible weight changes

Two deliberately adversarial re-weightings:

**W_B ΓÇö advisor-device-centric** (advisor_group_fit 0.30, publishability
0.15, novelty 0.15, evidence 0.10, schedule 0.10, cleanroom 0.05,
experimental 0.05, software 0.05, startup 0.05): OPT1 = 3.75, **OPT2 =
4.20**, OPT3 = 2.90, OPT4 = 3.15. OPT2 stays #1 even when the weighting is
tilted toward the axis where OPT1/OPT4 are strongest; OPT4 climbs to #3
but never becomes competitive.

**W_C ΓÇö graduation-speed-maximal** (publishability 0.30, schedule 0.15,
cleanroom 0.10, experimental 0.10, novelty 0.10, evidence 0.10, software
0.05, advisor 0.05, startup 0.05): OPT1 = 3.30, **OPT2 = 4.30**, OPT3 =
3.35, OPT4 = 2.30. OPT2 stays #1; OPT3 and OPT1 swap within the noise
band ΓÇö consistent with ┬º2.4's tie finding and with OPT3's role as the
schedule-driven fallback.

**Conclusion:** the OPT2 recommendation survives every plausible
re-weighting tried; only the #2/#3 ordering is weight-sensitive. For OPT2
to lose #1 under the baseline weights, its publishability and novelty
scores would both have to fall by ~2 points each ΓÇö the falsifiers that
would cause exactly that are named in ┬º11.

---

## 3. The options and the strongest defensible thesis for each

### 3.1 OPT1 ΓÇö Strengthened continuation (finished calibrated instrument, projects 02+03 as planned)

**Thesis:** *"The first absolutely calibrated multi-axis GaN Hall-effect
probe operated inside a stellarator, with in-vessel spinning-current
offset suppression and vector output validated against the computed
vacuum field"* ΓÇö project 03's own thesis statement (claim C020), executed
as written on the Aug/Nov 2026 campaign schedule.

**Why it is defensible:** it follows the exact validation paradigm the
field already accepts ΓÇö CTH's GaAs Hall array validated against
BiotΓÇôSavart vacuum-field predictions in a non-axisymmetric device
[S0143](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4894209) ΓÇö and lands in the genre (RSI
deployment+calibration+validation) where the ledger shows this work lives
([S0154](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0002193), [S0226], and RSI as the
ledger's most frequent venue, 29/231 rows).

**Why it is not the adopted framing:** every headline output is
campaign-coupled. The Nov 2026 machine time is, in project 03's own words,
"the immovable object"; bond yield on cube faces is its own top risk; and
the single-axis calibration that everything downstream assumes is still
blocked by the open ~109├ù anomaly (C017). Scored honestly, its
experimental burden (2) and schedule risk (2) are the worst of the three
viable options. Decision: **fold into OPT2** ΓÇö everything in OPT1 survives
as OPT2's hardware spine; what changes is that the thesis and the paper
portfolio no longer stand or fall with the campaign calendar.

### 3.2 OPT2 ΓÇö Adjusted continuation (calibrated output + system/software novelty layer) ΓÇö ADOPTED

**Thesis:** *"Absolutely calibrated GaN Hall-effect magnetic sensing in
the HSX stellarator, and a drift-corrected hybrid measurement architecture
that fuses direct (Hall) and inductive (pickup-coil) sensing ΓÇö upgrading
the 2025 uncalibrated single-axis demonstration into a traceable,
uncertainty-quantified, vector-capable diagnostic and quantifying what
direct sensing adds to a stellarator's existing magnetics."*

Concretely, OPT2 = OPT1's hardware spine plus four campaign-uncoupled work
packages, each answering a specific decline-letter item and each carrying
its own citable methodological precedent:

| Work package | Answers | Precedent / template | Campaign-dependent? |
|---|---|---|---|
| WP-A: GaN-vs-competitor comparison table | AEIC request (C010) | Assemblable from ledger rows; no published review contains it ΓÇö [S0065](https://doi.org/10.1088/2631-8695/ac0838) has no GaN row | No |
| WP-B: multi-die repeatability statistics (bench) | AEIC "only one module was tested" (C007/C010) | On-chip Hall-cell statistics [S0218](https://doi.org/10.3390/jsan2010085); JET's 18-sensor stability bar [S0068] | No |
| WP-C: absolute bench calibration + GUM/MC uncertainty budget | Reviewer 1 key point; AEIC minimum (C009/C010) | Traceable Hall calibration with written budget [S0051](https://doi.org/10.5194/jsss-9-391-2020); GUM/Monte-Carlo [S0220](https://doi.org/10.3390/s25051633); Allan-variance drift decomposition [S0168](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIM.2007.908635) | No |
| WP-D: hybrid Hall+inductive drift-corrected fusion on HSX data | The direction's core physics case | Kalman coil+Hall fusion at KSTAR [S0118](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/adb599); COMPASS-U/JET lineage [S0122](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fusengdes.2025.115180); non-fusion hybrid precedents [S0179](https://doi.org/10.3390/s22010182), [S0180](https://doi.org/10.3390/s19245455) | Partly (needs co-located coil data; existing 2025 data may partially serve) |

**Why this wins:** it is the only option that (a) closes every
decline-letter item, (b) puts claimed novelty at the granularity the
literature will defend (first GaN/WBG Hall in-vessel; first Hall of any
kind in a QHS stellarator; first quantified Hall-vs-inductive
complementarity study on a stellarator), (c) shifts a large fraction of
thesis work into software/analysis where the user wants it and where slip
risk is lowest, and (d) preserves every OPT1 deliverable as upside rather
than as a single point of failure.

### 3.3 OPT3 ΓÇö Genuine change of direction: software-only stellarator-magnetics methods

**Thesis (strongest honest version):** *"Physics-informed
machine-learning reconstruction of stellarator magnetic equilibria from
sparse magnetics, developed and benchmarked on HSX"* ΓÇö riding the
established method lineage: magnetics-only deep equilibrium solvers at
KSTAR [S0181](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/ab555f), stellarator-class
PINN/NN precedents at W7-X
[S0189](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/acc852),
[S0193](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/aab22d),
[S0194](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/ae2937),
[S0192](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0188634), and the V3FIT reconstruction
context HSX already uses
[S0132](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/55/11/113012). Digital-twin
reviews name sensor-integrated component-level twins as an open fusion gap
[S0196](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3561920),
[S0203](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/add16e).

**Why it loses now:** (a) the KSTAR-class precedent trained on 1,118
discharges [S0181]; no comparable HSX discharge-magnetics database was
found, and its existence is NOT ESTABLISHED FROM SUPPLIED FILES ΓÇö the
option's first months would be spent discovering whether it is feasible at
all; (b) advisor-group fit is the weakest of any option ΓÇö the Senesky
group's identity and co-authorship record are WBG devices
([S0004]ΓÇô[S0012]), not plasma-physics ML, so both supervision depth and
committee framing become risks; (c) it abandons the demonstrated in-vessel
asset and restarts reputation-building from zero with ~24 months left; (d)
its novelty is "first application of an established method to HSX" ΓÇö real
but incremental in a crowded ML-fusion field. Decision: **hold as
fallback** ΓÇö it is the named landing zone if the hardware premises fail
(┬º8, ┬º11), and OPT2's WP-D deliberately builds the data pipelines and
UW relationships that would make the landing survivable.

### 3.4 OPT4 ΓÇö Device-novelty escalation (considered and rejected)

The remaining pole of the option space: answer Reviewer 2 head-on with new
device topologies (three-terminal current-sensing GaN
[S0010](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3539435), AlN/GaN extreme-range
devices [S0012]) and a formal fusion-qualification program toward the
ITER/JET bar ([S0114], [S0068]). Rejected because: it maximizes cleanroom
burden against an explicit user constraint; qualification programs are
multi-year at institutional scale (ITER's OVSS campaign sat "at the limit
of technical feasibility" [S0148](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fusengdes.2021.112398));
its device-letter genre is exactly where the novelty attack succeeded; and
the mission scope forbids the radiation experiments such a program would
eventually demand. It is scored to show the boundary was examined, not as
a live candidate.

---

## 4. What is demonstrated, what requires analysis, what requires new experiment

**Already demonstrated (supplied facts, with claim IDs):**

- In-vessel deployment and survival of a packaged AlGaN/GaN Hall sensor in
  HSX across the Aug-2025 campaign, with shot-resolved transient response
  (C001, C002; raw data in `../../07_HSX_august2025_results/`).
- Temporal correlation of sensor output with the diamagnetic loop
  (manuscript Figs. 4ΓÇô5; C001ΓÇôC005).
- Readout chain: 200 V/V gain (C004); the 1 MHz bandwidth figure is
  asserted, reviewer-questioned, and has no derivation (C003).
- Four-phase spinning-current offset cancellation ΓëÑ130├ù ΓÇö **on a
  resistor-ring emulator only** (C016), with the ~109├ù magnitude anomaly
  open (C017). No calibration coefficient, V_off value, or absolute-field
  result exists for the real sensor (C005, C013, conflict C6).

**Requires analysis only (no new hardware, no campaign):**

- WP-A comparison table ΓÇö assembled from ledger rows ([S0006], [S0009],
  [S0011](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2024.3507799),
  [S0014](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2014.2368074),
  [S0016](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6501/ac12fe),
  [S0017](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2201339); metadata-only rows
  re-confirmed against primary PDFs first, per the Stage 10D gate).
- Bandwidth derivation for the existing chain (C003) ΓÇö analysis plus at
  most a bench frequency sweep; norm: [S0076](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3246785).
- Re-analysis of the 68-shot 2025 dataset in field units *once* WP-C
  yields a calibration (Fig. 5 conversion the AEIC requested).
- WP-D algorithm development against synthetic/emulator data and any
  already-recorded HSX coil signals (availability of co-located records is
  an Unresolved gate ΓÇö UW ask, ┬º10).

**Requires new experiment (bench, no campaign):**

- Resolution of the ~109├ù anomaly (╬öV gain check ΓÇö already project 02's
  named top priority; a Proposed experiment inherited, not invented here).
- WP-C: Helmholtz calibration of the real GaN die; temperature
  coefficient; overnight drift; Allan-variance characterization.
- WP-B: raw-offset and sensitivity statistics across ΓëÑ3 packaged dies
  (project 02's static-bias mode is the ready tool; die count is an
  advisor question, ┬º10).

**Requires HSX campaign (upside, not single-point-of-failure):**

- In-situ absolute anchor vs computed vacuum field (coil-only shots) ΓÇö
  the [S0143] paradigm; campaign #1 (Aug 2026) target.
- Co-located Hall vs B-dot/pickup comparison (Reviewer 1's alternative
  ask, C009) and WP-D's in-vessel validation.
- Vector-probe deployment and component-resolved dynamics (campaign #2) ΓÇö
  the OPT1/RSI centerpiece, per
  [`../../03_HSX_Vector_Probe_RSI2026/docs/rsi_experiment_and_publication_plan.md`](../../03_HSX_Vector_Probe_RSI2026/docs/rsi_experiment_and_publication_plan.md).

---

## 5. Novelty versus prior art

**The defensible claims (each bounded by named prior art):**

1. *First GaN/AlGaN (WBG 2DEG) Hall sensor operated in-vessel in any
   magnetic-confinement device* ΓÇö absence finding, three independent
   lanes; bounded by the mature non-GaN fusion Hall lineage: CASTOR
